title: Scripture and Prayer
definition: Scripture and prayer belong together because God speaks through His Word and His people respond to Him in dependence, confession, worship, and request.
summary: Prayerful Bible reading keeps study from becoming cold information and keeps prayer anchored in God's revealed truth.
christFocus: Christ teaches His people to abide in His words and ask in dependence upon Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture and Prayer teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to scripture and prayer by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
